question: Should `typingTtlSeconds` be a single user-facing typing-lifetime contract that also governs Discord’s independent 20-minute cap, or should OpenClaw retain a documented Discord-specific safety ceiling?
rationale: The patch adds a durable public config/default surface, but the correct relation between the generic stale-refresh TTL and Discord’s run-lifetime safety guard is a product and channel-policy choice rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Make the setting govern Discord
options.body: Wire the resolved TTL into Discord’s duration behavior, preserving an explicit stale/orphan safeguard and adding long-run lifecycle tests.

options.title: Retain a Discord safety ceiling
options.body: Keep the independent cap but document the upper bound and validate configuration so users are not led to expect unsupported durations.

options.title: Defer the new setting
options.body: Close or pause the configuration addition until maintainers choose the intended cross-channel typing contract.

recommendation.title: Make the setting govern Discord
recommendation.body: Wire the resolved TTL into Discord’s duration behavior, preserving an explicit stale/orphan safeguard and adding long-run lifecycle tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature-history signal most directly connects this person to Discord’s long-running typing lifecycle and safety cap.
